en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the House-Hall, 44.
The Training Rule on Service for Laypeople:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were performing services for householders.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... were indignant, complained, and grumbled, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs perform services for householders?"... [and so on].
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs are performing services for householders?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
“How indeed, monks, can nuns perform services for householders?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...
And so, monks, let the nuns recite this training rule:”
“Whatever nun should perform domestic services for a layperson, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Regarding “whatever nun”: whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Service for a layperson" means:
If she cooks rice porridge, a meal, or solid food for a householder, or washes a garment or a turban, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense in the case of drinking rice porridge.
If, for the sake of the Saṅgha’s meal,
for the worship of a cetiya,
or for her own personal attendant, she cooks rice gruel, a meal, or fresh food; or if she washes a garment or a turban;
"An insane woman," "one who is a first-offender.
The fourth training rule is concluded.
